description: RNA interference in the native fern gives an arsenite-sensitive phenotype and the gene rescues an ACR3-deficient yeast, while the transgene confers large shoot arsenic accumulation in rice in two independent settings (https://doi.org/10.1105/tpc.109.069773, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eehl.2025.100168).
No animal work exists. Mammalian cells have no vacuole and detoxify arsenic by AS3MT methylation and export, so a human version would need lysosomal retargeting that nobody has tried.
Transport activity and vacuolar localisation are established, but the ten-transmembrane architecture rests on homology and AlphaFold models with no experimental structure.
No direct lifespan effect expected
Two parrot species, allele-specific expression and a yeast knockout/knock-in reconstitution all point at the same enzymatic step (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adp7710).
No mammalian work exists, the causal variant is non-coding and regulatory, and in humans loss of this enzyme causes Sjogren-Larsson syndrome.

The conversion was demonstrated qualitatively by mass spectrometry with no reported conversion percentage or kinetic constants, and the lead variant matched phenotype in 98% of individuals rather than all.

The lipoprotein-lipase and endothelial-lipase de-repression mechanism is well established, and GalNAc-mediated hepatocyte entry is directly demonstrated by a ligand-density titration (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-37465-1).
Editing is in Phase 1 with safety as the primary endpoint; no human efficacy or outcome data exist, and primate durability is proven only to six months.

Loss-of-function carriers in over 45,000 sequenced participants show the lipid phenotype with protein-level confirmation of haploinsufficiency, and two Phase 1 editing trials are dosing patients (https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1612790).
Cardiovascular outcome trials for apoC-III lowering have not reported, so the hard-event benefit remains a property of the lifelong germline allele rather than a demonstrated drug effect.

Two independent cohorts totalling more than 180,000 people agree on both the lipid effect (39% and 44% lower triglycerides) and the cardiovascular effect (40% and 41% risk reductions), with genotype-first design removing most confounding.
An FDA-approved drug (olezarsen, TRYNGOLZA) and a second marketed agent by an independent modality (plozasiran, RNA interference) already reproduce the knockdown in patients.
The Christchurch APOE variant delayed Alzheimer onset by decades in a human PSEN1 carrier; editing reverses pathology in human neurons and mice but has not been delivered across a living human brain.
Well-established mammalian aquaporin biology
Enhancement is species-specific; not directly translatable
No ASGR1-directed drug or editor has reached a registered trial, and no homozygous-null human has ever been described, so the full knockout is uncharacterised.

The association and its pharmacodynamic marker are solid, but no experiment yet shows how losing a desialylated-glycoprotein receptor lowers non-HDL cholesterol; the pathway is proposed, not demonstrated.

Two independent loss-of-function alleles in the same gene, over 390,000 genomes, and coronary-disease replication across eight populations with a heterogeneity P value of 0.96 (https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1508419).

argument: mouse three-factor in vivo (cells, not hearing)
description: Avian hair-cell regeneration is a replicated 1988 finding, and adult-mouse ATOH1+GFI1+POU4F3 reprogramming is lineage-traced and quantified along the organ of Corti versus single-factor ATOH1. New hair cells appear; functional hearing restoration in mammals is not established.

The only clinical test, Novartis CGF166 (NCT02132130), delivered single-factor ATOH1 and left treated-ear thresholds 8.5 dB worse at week 52. No three-factor (ATOH1+GFI1+POU4F3) candidate has entered humans, and no restored hearing threshold exists in any mammal. Mammalian enhancement potential for a human ear is Low until a three-factor human trial shows benefit.
The ATOH1/GFI1/POU4F3 hierarchy of hair-cell specification is well mapped and the regenerated cells express the expected marker set, but PRESTIN and bundle maturation are incomplete.
Strong evidence in yeast and in vitro systems
Modest protection, osmotic-shock-specific, not true drying
Gene transfer cannot build gecko setae: the trait is a morphogenetic skin structure, not a soluble protein phenotype.
Cholesteryl-ester shuttling from HDL to apoB-containing lipoproteins is long-established biochemistry, and truncating variants are an unambiguous read-out of complete loss.

No gene-directed program exists, the LDL and triglyceride arms are only marginally significant, and the pharmacological phenocopy increased mortality in one large outcome trial and failed for futility in two more.
Protein-truncating CETP variants in humans raise HDL, lower LDL, and reduce coronary-disease odds; the genetic phenotype works in people even though drug phenocopies failed.
13+ independent convergent evolution events validate the single-aa edit
No CRISPR/base-editing demonstration yet; natural variants only

argument: human cell repair (no in vivo mammal)
description: Transient transfection of cultured human cells improved DSB repair ~1.6× (Firsanov 2025 Nature). Lifespan extension is Drosophila-only (~20%). No mouse or human in vivo trial. Extracellular CIRBP (eCIRP) is a known inflammatory DAMP in sepsis, so systemic overexpression safety is unresolved.

Chlorotoxin is a deathstalker peptide developed as a glioma-targeting / surgical imaging agent (TM-601 Phase I/II; tozuleristide fluorescence). That is cancer medicine, not a body enhancement. No enhancement phenotype (strength, senses, longevity, regeneration, stress resistance) is claimed or shown in mammals.
Phase I/II human clinical trials completed; FDA orphan drug designation
Transgenic mice showed powerful skin cancer resistance
Marsupial photolyase mRNA functional in human keratinocytes (Boros 2013)

Sufficiency of the two-enzyme pair is shown by mass spectrometry against an authentic astaxanthin standard, across three different carotenoid substrates, with a negative-control partner enzyme that fails (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2022.08.013).
No mammal has ever carried this pathway, mammalian skin lacks carotenoid-storing pigment cells, and the product canthaxanthin has documented retinal crystal deposition in humans taking it orally.

A transgenic fish visibly converts its yellow pigment cells to reddish-orange, but the generality of the pathway is contested: house finch red plumage does not use it (https://doi.org/10.1111/mec.17744).

Chromosomal expression of ectABC gave a clean gain of salt tolerance in a cyanobacterium of a different phylum, with survival at an otherwise lethal 500 mM NaCl (https://doi.org/10.3389/fmicb.2023.1123081).
Human data support the molecule applied topically, not the genes: no human cell has expressed ectABC, and mammals have no ectoine transporter to fall back on.
The three-step enzymology and the preferential-exclusion physics of ectoine as a compatible solute are settled, and the pathway has been reconstituted heterologously.
Specific causal variant not yet identified
Tibetan EPAS1 haplotype carriers at altitude have ~0.8 g/dL lower hemoglobin — a replicated human physiological phenotype.
The FGF18-FGFR3-SOX9 anabolic axis in chondrocytes is well characterised and mechanistically distinct from the FGFR1 catabolic arm.
The 0.05 mm gain produced no WOMAC improvement at two years, two cartilage-repair trials were terminated, and no phase 3 has been started.
Sprifermin (FGF18) met its quantitative-MRI cartilage-thickness primary endpoint in a 549-patient randomised phase 2 trial.

No peer-reviewed autonomous bioluminescent mammalian germline line. Mammals lack the caffeic-acid pathway that fungal/plant autonomous systems need, so self-glow without injected luciferin remains blocked.

Transgenic luciferase mice are a standard in-vivo imaging tool (IVIS after IP D-luciferin; de Wet 1987 onward). Mammalian function with injected substrate is established. Not High/Very High as an enhancement: it is a reporter, not a body upgrade, and clinical human imaging uses PET instead.
Uncertain whether gain-of-function variants can be transferred
FOXO3 longevity alleles are associated with extreme survival across multiple independent human cohorts.

Minicircle/BioViva sell FST gene therapy commercially in Prospera/Dubai (unregulated). Distinct from Mendell disease trials; independent evidence that the clinic product improves healthy-adult muscle/performance is lacking.

AAV1-FST344 improved 6-minute walk distance in Becker muscular dystrophy and inclusion-body myositis patients in peer-reviewed Mendell trials (2015/2017). Independent human clinical efficacy for the disease indication.
GFP is routinely expressed in mammalian cells and transgenic mammals as a fluorescent reporter; it is not used as an in-vivo human clinical enhancer.

Growth hormone receptor loss collapsing hepatic IGF-1 and downstream RAS, PKA and TOR signalling is the best-conserved longevity pathway in biology, with serum-transfer experiments in human mammary epithelial cells supporting the apoptosis arm.
No therapeutic pursues this direction, the morphological cost is inseparable from the benefit, and no lifespan extension was measured in the cohort itself.

A 22-year prospective cohort with 1,606 related controls sharing genes and environment, reporting zero diabetes in 90 subjects and cancer absent as a cause of death at any age (https://doi.org/10.1126/scitranslmed.3001845).

HKT transporters have no metazoan orthologue and animals have no xylem, so the trait cannot be transferred to a human body as designed; only the general principle of compartment-level ion interception carries over.
Sodium-selective uniport by HKT1-subfamily transporters is well established functionally, but no experimental structure of TmHKT1;5-A exists and PDB 8W9T belongs to the other subfamily.

The causal gene was mapped, localised to root cells surrounding the xylem, and validated in saline field trials against near-isogenic durum lines with grain yield as the endpoint (https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.2120).

argument: insect cell line only (no mammalian transfer)
description: HSF1 knockdown in Polypedilum vanderplanki cells cut desiccation survival ~5-fold (Mazin 2018). No mammalian HSF1_pv construct has been built or tested. Human HSF1 overexpression is linked to tumour growth — not an enhancement safety signal. Primary must not exceed Medium while evidence is insect-cell-only.
Disaggregase activity, the two- to four-fold rise in ATP hydrolysis on potentiation, and the substrate-selection change are directly measured, and multiple cryo-EM structures of the hexamer exist.
No mammalian in vivo efficacy, no immunogenicity data for a foreign hexameric ATPase, unsolved delivery to post-mitotic neurons, and off-target unfolding that appears at 37 degrees C.

Quantified rescue of alpha-synuclein, TDP-43 and FUS proteotoxicity in yeast and protection of dopaminergic neurons in C. elegans at two time points, but the animal evidence is a single invertebrate model.
Completely novel sensory modality; no mammalian neural circuitry exists
BK channel well-studied; skate variant expressed in human HEK293 cells
Single study in mice
Minicircle Prospera phase-1 plasmid Klotho reports dose-dependent serum α-Klotho upregulation (company data). Not independently peer-reviewed efficacy for cognition or aging endpoints.

KL-VS haplotype carriers show cognitive benefits in humans; therapeutic protein and gene-therapy programs are in human trials/clinic use, while the mouse lifespan gain remains a separate mammal-only claim.
Strong evidence in young mouse tissue repair
No evidence for adult limb or organ regeneration

A single injection more than doubled median lifespan in a genetically faithful mouse model of the human disease, with a matching histological rescue of the aorta (Koblan 2021, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-03086-7).
No human editing trial exists, dual-AAV9 dosing has not been scaled to a child, and pre-existing AAV9 immunity would exclude some patients.
Correction of 87–91% of the pathogenic allele in two independent patient fibroblast lines, with indels at or below 0.15% and no off-target DNA or RNA editing detected.
No human tissue expression; spinning requires shear forces not available in vivo
Expressed in 7+ organisms including transgenic goats and silkworms

Adhesion energy on mica was measured directly with a surface forces apparatus on native purified protein, and the DOPA-dependence of the effect is reproduced across laboratories (https://doi.org/10.1021/bi3002538).
No mammal has been engineered to secrete the protein from its epidermis; every quoted number comes from purified protein between mineral surfaces.
Recombinant mussel adhesive protein is sold as a research reagent and coating, but there is no approved clinical product and no trial administering it.
Radiosynthesis claim poorly supported
Small n, historical controls
MGMT-P140K chemoprotection showed peer-reviewed human clinical efficacy in autologous CD34+ gene therapy for glioblastoma (Adair 2012).
A human child with natural myostatin loss-of-function had roughly double-normal quadriceps cross-section; mouse knockouts confirm the mammal muscle phenotype.
Heterologous expression in yeast reconstituted psittacofulvin synthesis, with products matched to feather pigments by mass spectrometry.
No mammalian expression has been attempted, no titre is reported, and the phenotype depends on a feather-epithelial regulatory context that has not been rebuilt.

A single coding variant segregated completely with plumage colour in 280 genotyped budgerigars, and mapping independently localised the locus at p = 10^-72 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.08.016).
The NGF-TrkA/p75NTR axis and the epithelium-nerve trophic loop in the cornea are well characterised, and the readouts are lesion closure and corneal sensitivity rather than surrogate markers.
Efficacy is established specifically for trigeminal-denervation keratitis; extension to persistent epithelial defects of other cause and to optic neuropathy is still in recruiting phase 3 trials.

Two independent double-masked vehicle-controlled randomised trials met their corneal-healing endpoints, a meta-analysis of both gives moderate GRADE certainty and an NNT of 3, and the drug is approved and marketed in the EU and US.

The three-enzyme route from zeaxanthin to dihydrogalloxanthin was reconstituted stepwise in HEK293 cells and the products identified chromatographically, matching the apocarotenoids measured in real cone oil droplets.
Mammalian cones have no oil droplet to hold the filter, human vision has no fourth cone class for it to serve, and unsequestered carotenoid accumulation is cytotoxic in mouse and zebrafish.

The functional payoff is modelled rather than measured: droplet cutoffs and discriminable-colour counts come from receptor-noise modelling on 18 species' measured optics, and no animal has been engineered to test them.

Testicular growth under short-wavelength light in quail whose eyes were patched and pineal removed is a clean whole-animal demonstration that light is being read inside the brain; the evidence comes from one laboratory and one publication.
Two independent action-spectrum experiments on heterologously expressed quail OPN5 agreed to within 1 nm (419 and 418 nm), establishing the molecule as a violet-sensitive, retinal-based photopigment.

No mammalian hypothalamus has been made light-sensitive with OPN5, and a human skull and scalp attenuate hardest at the receptor's ~420 nm peak, so photon delivery rather than the protein is the blocking problem.

Vision recovered behaviourally and electrophysiologically in a glaucoma model treated after damage was established, with a doubling of retinal ganglion cell survival after nerve crush in middle-aged mice (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2975-4).

A first-in-human Phase 1 is recruiting with 18 participants and safety as the primary endpoint, no efficacy data exist in humans, and visual acuity restoration failed in 18-month-old mice (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07290244).

The effect is genetically pinned to TET1/TET2-dependent active demethylation and requires polycistronic co-delivery, but the causal CpG sites among the 1,226-site signature are not individually validated.

Colour-opponent responses were recorded directly from native photoreceptors in the lizard parietal eye, so the phenotype exists in a real cell in a real animal; it rests on a single founding electrophysiology study rather than on independent functional replication.
No mammalian cell has ever been given this opsin pair, and the cascade uses G proteins absent from vertebrate rods and cones, so there is no host circuit to receive its output.

The 522 nm absorption maximum was measured on purified recombinant pigment and reproduced in a second lizard species by a separate group, with photosensitivity and extinction coefficient quantified against a bovine rhodopsin standard.
Human PCSK9 LOF carriers have substantially lower LDL and coronary disease; VERVE-102 base editing cut LDL 39–55% in a human trial.
The phenotype is unambiguous in the native animal, months of activity under total anoxia, and the closely related common carp provides a natural negative control.

The pathway has never been expressed in another animal, it needs muscle-restricted stoichiometry rather than plain overexpression, the enabling substitution is a human disease allele, and a land animal has no way to excrete the ethanol.

The decarboxylase activity, the more than 60-fold muscle-specific E1 excess and the effect of betaD319N on E1-E2 binding are documented, but the reaction was not reconstituted from purified carp enzymes.
2021 Nobel Prize for Piezo discovery; human LOF mutations confirm essential role in touch/proprioception
No overexpression studies; GOF mutations cause distal arthrogryposis in humans
Nacre uses aragonite; vertebrate bone uses hydroxyapatite — different mineral system
RNAi + CRISPR validated in pearl oyster; essential for nacre

uPAR-positive cells account for 67–90% of the senescent burden in aged liver, and an independent group replicated senescent-cell clearance with an unrelated antigen in aged nonhuman primates (https://doi.org/10.1126/scitranslmed.add1951).

No senolytic CAR T cell has entered a human trial, the protocol requires cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion at 200 mg/kg, and the antigen is shared with activated immune cells and invasive tumour cells.

A single infusion improved glucose handling and exercise capacity in 20-month-old mice with the correct age-specificity control, and cleared senescent cells in two independent liver models (https://doi.org/10.1038/s43587-023-00560-5, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2403-9).
Poor translational outlook for rejuvenation
Limited biochemical evidence
One-lab mouse data; moderate effect; not independently replicated
In Escherichia coli the pump substituted for a chemically poisoned respiratory chain in both a colony-survival assay and a tethered-cell flagellar assay (https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0611035104).
No mammalian in vivo data. The only metazoan work targets different archaeal rhodopsins to mitochondria in flies and worms, all of it retinal-dependent, and green light does not penetrate tissue.

Light-driven, retinal-dependent proton translocation by proteorhodopsin is established by spectroscopy, by solution NMR and cryo-EM structures, and by direct proton-motive-force measurement in single cells.
Confidence in ultrasonic-hearing connection is declining

The glucosylation step, the stabilised variant's melting-temperature gain and the 65% conversion of 100 mM indoxyl were all measured directly on purified enzyme (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-45749-3).
No plant or animal host has been engineered with the stabilised enzyme; the trait exists as an in vitro process and a lab dyeing protocol.
Environmental and cost advantages come from a life-cycle and techno-economic model on the European grid mix, with UDP-glucose recycling modelled rather than demonstrated at scale.
Nature 2015 with survival data in two disease models
All key data from single laboratory (MRC Prion Unit)
No expression in any vertebrate tissue; cross-linking mechanism untested in vivo
90-97% resilience demonstrated in recombinant material; active tissue engineering R&D

Purified enzyme measurably suppresses double-strand breakage at 90 C, and the authors show the activity is independent of both ATP hydrolysis and positive supercoiling (https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkh683).

Loss-of-function evidence spans three archaeal genera and three methods — deletion in Pyrococcus, disruption in Thermococcus and CRISPR interference in Sulfolobus — and consistently defines a temperature threshold near 90 C.

No eukaryotic expression has ever been attempted, the protective effect is gated above 90 C, the coding sequence is near the single-AAV packaging ceiling, and positive supercoiling runs counter to human topoisomerase activity.
Two independent host species, tobacco and cotton, show the same physiological signature, and the cotton work reaches field-scale yield endpoints across multiple papers.
The reaction is standard, well-understood NAD(P)+-dependent aldehyde oxidation, and the transgenic plants show the predicted fall in malondialdehyde and hydrogen peroxide.
No animal or mammalian-cell expression exists, and in a human the same chemistry overlaps ALDH2, which handles acetaldehyde from alcohol and retinaldehyde.
No animal carries this allele; there is no lifespan, healthspan or tumour-incidence measurement for it, and the two linked substitutions have never been separated.
The centenarian enrichment is 1% versus 0.5% at P = 0.3, and no company or trial is pursuing the allele.

Multiple orthogonal assays agree — enzymology, double-strand break repair reporters, γH2AX foci, LINE1 silencing and cancer cell apoptosis all point the same way in human cells (https://doi.org/10.15252/embj.2021110393).
No ZnT8 inhibitor exists in the clinic and no company has disclosed a candidate, so the phenotype is currently only available to people born with it.

The link from reduced granule zinc to increased insulin secretion is inferred from human physiology rather than demonstrated, and mouse knockouts gave heterogeneous results that contradict the human phenotype.

Two independent large-scale sequencing studies agree, and the 2025 cohort includes 18 complete human knockouts whose recall-by-genotype glucose tolerance tests show the predicted gene-dose effect (https://doi.org/10.1007/s00125-025-06530-3).
Essential for planarian regeneration
Unlikely to transfer regeneration to mammals
No mammalian cell or animal has ever expressed superoxide reductase, the cofactor-recycling requirement in a mammalian cytosol is untested, and the reaction hands the tissue extra hydrogen peroxide.
Gain-of-function heat and oxidative-stress tolerance was quantified in two transgenic plant species, but both studies come from a single laboratory lineage with no independent replication.
The enzyme, its reaction stoichiometry and its electron-donor chain were characterised directly, and three experimental crystal structures of the iron active site exist.
Genetic knockout and antibody pharmacology agree in mouse, and the phenotype reproduced in a diphyodont non-rodent (ferret) with human-like dentition and micro-CT confirmation.
USAG-1 is a defined secreted BMP and Wnt antagonist, the operative arm was isolated by epitope-specific antibodies, and pSMAD1/5/8 staining confirms BMP signalling in the induced tooth.

A humanised antibody with Japanese orphan designation is in Phase 1 safety testing, but no human efficacy exists, positional control is unsolved and the presence of dormant buds in patients is inferred rather than imaged.
Well-characterized molecular mechanism
Female-only, small cohort
Spectral-tuning substitutions are mapped, but no mammalian in-vivo test of a UV-shifted SWS1 opsin has been reported.
Captive and wild hummingbirds behaved as the receptor pharmacology predicts, rejecting water within three or four licks and rejecting the artificial sweeteners the receptor does not recognise.
The receptor has never been placed in an animal's taste buds, and human T1R1-T1R3 feeds a circuit already labelled savoury, so the perceptual outcome of the swap is untested.

Chimera mapping narrowed sugar responsiveness from a whole domain to 109 residues and then to 19 non-consecutive positions, with the negative result that subsets fail; the assay was repeated across the hummingbird radiation in 2022.
No engineering attempts to evaluate

AAV9-TERT extended median lifespan in 1- and 2-year-old mice (+24% / +13%) without increased cancer incidence in the Blasco lab studies. Mammalian in-vivo benefit is clear; independent human efficacy is not.

AAV-TERT has been sold/administered commercially (BioViva; company claims 300+ patients) and in criticized Libella trials. No peer-reviewed validation of benefit; scientific skepticism is high. Human exposure without independent proof of effect.

Tensile properties, slime volume and thread storage density have been measured directly in Eptatretus stoutii by independent groups (https://doi.org/10.1016/S0006-3495(03)74629-3, https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.81405).
No transgenic animal, no commercial material, and thread-keratin genes appear absent from amniote genomes entirely.
Recombinant thread proteins can be expressed and spun, but the fibres land at 10^2-10^3 kPa, three to four orders of magnitude below native thread (https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.5c13031).
Multiple independent mouse gene therapy studies; clinical pipeline active
No study tests TMC1 overexpression above wild-type levels
Strong phenotypic evidence in elephants
Less certain about cross-species causal mechanism
Never tested in elephant cells
Triggers apoptosis in TP53-null/mutant human cancer lines in culture; never tested in a mouse, normal tissue, or elephant cell.
Viper TRPA1 IR tuning is characterized in snake neurons and heterologous channels; no mammal has been shown to gain infrared sensing from the variant.

The repertoire is documented by deep sequencing of the native organ with conservative similarity thresholds, and independent genome annotations in python, garter snake and anole reproduce the same V2R-rich, V1R-poor pattern.
Essentially no snake V2R has a known ligand and none has been tested in a heterologous functional assay, so the receptors' chemistry is inferred from family membership rather than measured.
A human has a vestigial vomeronasal organ, no accessory olfactory bulb and no forked tongue, so the receptor bank would have neither an epithelium to sit in nor a circuit to read it.

argument: human clinic exposure (safety acceptable; efficacy unproven)
description: Unlimited Bio sells VEGF gene therapy commercially in Prospera ZEDE (Honduras) under light special-zone regulation (not FDA/EMA). Human exposure is real: in known practitioner circles, no serious side effects have been reported. Independent peer-reviewed proof that the enhancement package works as marketed is still missing — High for human safety exposure, not Very High for efficacy.

Euroinject One (2005) found no significant myocardial perfusion improvement vs placebo despite some wall-motion signals. Cardiac VEGF GT efficacy is unsettled; do not equate PAD/CLI positives with heart-failure/angina certainty.

Human VEGF gene therapy has shown clinical benefit in limb ischemia / PAD: early Isner/Losordo CLI and angina positives, and Russian Neovasculgen (plasmid VEGF) improved pain-free walking distance with marketed use for PAD. That is peer-reviewed / approved-path human efficacy for a vascular indication — Very High for mammalian/human enhancement potential of the pathway. Cardiac results are mixed (Euroinject One negative for myocardial perfusion); Prospera clinic sales are a High secondary (human exposure with acceptable safety; enhancement efficacy still unproven).
